newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels dynamite pipeline for 31st time.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels dynamite pipeline for 31st time.

text.p: Leftist rebels have dynamited Colombia's main oil pipeline for the 31st time this year, a spokeswoman for the state oil company Ecopetrol said Wednesday.
The amount of crude oil lost in the blast on Tuesday evening near the town of Cubara in central Boyaca province was not immediately known.

Oil pumping was suspended along the pipeline that transports about 200,000 barrels per day from the Cano Limon field, operated by U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum Corp in eastern Arauca province, to the Caribbean port of Covenas.
The attack was thought to be the work of the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla force, which specialises in attacks on oil infrastructure, military sources said.
About 99,000 barrels of crude have been spilled in this year's attacks on the pipeline, the Ecopetrol spokeswoman said. The cost of the damage has not been calculated.

The pipeline was blown up 47 times last year and more than 105,000 barrels of crude were spilled. The cost of the environmental clean-up, repairs and the value of lost crude was put at about $9.3 million.
